sections.heading: Introduction to Machine Learning & Supervised Learning

bullets.text: Machine Learning teaches computers to learn from data, not explicit rules.
Supervised learning trains systems on labeled data.
Example: an email marked as spam or not spam.
Common algorithms include decision trees, support vector machines, and neural networks.
System finds patterns in data without labels.
Example: clustering customers based on purchasing behavior.
K-means is a classic unsupervised learning algorithm.
An agent interacts with an environment.
Examples: training AI to play video games or control a robot.
Overfitting: model memorizes training data, performs poorly on new data.
Bias: occurs when the training data itself is not balanced.
Self-driving cars: utilized for object recognition.
